title: _claimRewards underflows and reverts after pauseWithdraw -> unpause -> claim sequence, bricking the user's reward-claim and normal withdraw paths
rootCause: `pauseWithdraw` decrements `user.amount` and `totalStaked` but does NOT rebase `user.phUSDDebt` / `user.stableDebt`. On subsequent `unpause` + `claim` (or `withdraw`/`stake`), `_claimRewards` computes `pendingPhUSDAmount = (user.amount * accPhUSDPerShare) / PRECISION - user.phUSDDebt`. Because `user.amount` was reduced while `user.{phUSD,stable}Debt` was anchored to the larger pre-pause amount and an earlier `accX` checkpoint, the new product can be strictly less than the stale debt, triggering Solidity 0.8 checked subtraction underflow and reverting the entire call.
impact: After legitimately recovering principal via `pauseWithdraw`, the user is permanently unable to call `claim`, `withdraw(amount < user.amount)`, or `stake(amount, recipient = victim)` on their remaining position: every path that reaches `_claimRewards` reverts. The view helpers `pendingPhUSD(user)` and `pendingStable(user)` also revert, breaking front-end displays. Only remaining principal-recovery path is `withdraw(user.amount)` -- which also reverts because it too runs `_claimRewards` first -- so the user must wait for the next pause and call `pauseWithdraw(user.amount)` again to finally exit. Pending phUSD and stable rewards earned prior to the partial pauseWithdraw are silently forfeited.
attackVector: No attacker required; reachable by any honest user who partially escapes during a pause. Concrete sequence: (1) user stakes; (2) accumulator funds rewards via `collectReward`; (3) time passes, `accPhUSDPerShare` and `accStablePerShare` grow; (4) user claims so `user.{phUSD,stable}Debt` is set to a non-trivial value; (5) pauser pauses the contract; (6) user calls `pauseWithdraw(part)`; (7) pauser unpauses; (8) user calls `claim()` -> revert (Panic 0x11). A malicious or merely-careless pauser can be combined with normal user behavior to brick positions at scale.
steps: collectReward(R), advance time by Δt so accStablePerShare and accPhUSDPerShare both rise
claim() -- user.amount=100e18, user.phUSDDebt and user.stableDebt now equal (100e18 * accX) / PRECISION
pauser.pause(); user.pauseWithdraw(50e18) -- user.amount drops to 50e18, debts unchanged
pauser.unpause(); user.claim() -- _claimRewards computes (50e18 * accPhUSDPerShare)/PRECISION which is ~half of user.phUSDDebt, triggers underflow on subtraction, REVERTS
remediation: Either (a) in `pauseWithdraw`, proportionally reduce `user.phUSDDebt` and `user.stableDebt` so the invariant `(user.amount * accX)/PRECISION >= user.XDebt` is preserved (e.g. multiply each debt by `(user.amount - amount) / user.amount` before assigning); or (b) in `_claimRewards`, clamp the subtraction (`pending = a > b ? a - b : 0`) to make the path forfeit pending rewards rather than revert; or (c) call `_updatePool` + `_claimRewards` inside `pauseWithdraw` so debts are rebased atomically before the principal cut.
profileReference: Profile §4.3 (pauseWithdraw worked-case 2 final paragraph), §7 V2, §8.2; flagged for code-scanner reachability confirmation in §12.
